mainTopic: Proper use of פסוקים, whispering and remedies, demons, and the value of suffering at רבי אליעזר's sickbed
overview: The amud opens by finishing the reading of 'כל ימי עני רעים' as describing a narrow-minded person. It then explains, through שמואל's rule that a change in routine makes the stomach sick, why even a poor man's שבת and יום טוב are bad days for him. A ברייתא warns that turning פסוקים into party songs brings evil to the world, while a פסוק said at its proper time brings good. The גמרא returns to the משנה about whispering over a wound: רבי יוחנן limits it to one who spits, and רב and רבי חנינא extend it even to פסוקים without ה׳'s name. Next come ברייתות about soothing actions on שבת, consulting demons, and whispering over oil, illustrated by two stories of harm and rescue. רבי יוחנן's reading of 'כי אני ה׳ רפאך' shows that ה׳ heals even when He sends illness. The amud ends with two accounts of רבי אליעזר's illness, where רבי עקיבא teaches that suffering is precious. His proof from King מנשה begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Narrow mind versus broad mind
steps.stepSummary: The interpretation of the פסוק in משלי concludes: 'all the days of the poor are bad' describes a person with a narrow mind, and 'a good heart is always a feast' describes a person with a broad mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'All the days of the poor are bad' refers to someone whose mind is narrow. 'And for the good-hearted it is always a feast' refers to someone whose mind is broad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation, begun on the previous page, of the two halves of a פסוק in משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read as describing temperament, not money. Someone with a דעת קצרה cannot accept things that go against his wishes, so every day feels bad. Someone with a דעת רחבה accepts what happens, so life feels like a constant feast.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind is narrow: he can't tolerate things that go against his will
His mind is broad: he is tolerant and easygoing

phrases.english: (this is) one whose mind is narrow.
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from the previous page: 'כל ימי עני רעים' refers to this kind of person.

phrases.english: "And for the good-hearted it is always a feast"
this is one whose mind is broad.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטוֹב לֵב מִשְׁתֶּה תָמִיד זֶה שֶׁדַּעְתּוֹ רְחָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an explanation of the פסוק begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two halves of the פסוק describe a narrow-minded person and a broad-minded person.

steps.title: Doesn't a poor person have שבת and יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי questions the plain reading of 'all the days of the poor are bad': a poor man has שבתות and ימים טובים, which are good days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said about 'All the days of the poor are bad': But there are שבתות and ימים טובים!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי challenges the word 'all' in the פסוק. On שבת and יום טוב even a poor man rests and eats well, so how can all his days be bad?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסוק is read about a poor person in the literal sense. The problem is the word כל: there seem to be clear exceptions every week and every festival.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
"All the days of the poor are bad."
But aren't there Sabbaths and festivals?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיכָּא שַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes up the same פסוק, now read literally about a poor person, and questions it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'all' in 'כל ימי עני רעים'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבת and יום טוב are pleasant days even for a poor man, so not all his days are bad.

steps.title: A change in routine makes the poor man sick
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with שמואל's rule: a change in one's usual routine is the start of stomach illness, so even the poor man's festive days hurt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like שמואל, for שמואל said: a change in routine is the beginning of intestinal illness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting שמואל: a sudden change in how a person eats makes his stomach sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor man usually eats very little. When he suddenly eats rich meals on שבת and יום טוב, the change itself upsets his stomach, so even those days turn out bad for him. That keeps the word 'all' in the פסוק true.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with what שמואל said
A change in one's regular routine

phrases.english: As Shmuel said, for Shmuel said:
A change in routine is the beginning of intestinal illness.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an outside principle that turns the apparent exception into part of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת and יום טוב are good days for a poor man.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sudden change in his diet makes him ill, so even those days are bad for him.
steps.whatToRemember: 'כל ימי עני רעים' is read two ways: as a narrow-minded person, or as a truly poor man whose rare feasts upset his routine (שמואל's שינוי וסת).

steps.title: Using פסוקים as entertainment brings evil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that singing a פסוק of שיר השירים as a secular song, or reciting a פסוק at a feast out of its proper time, brings evil to the world, because the תורה complains before הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who reads a פסוק of שיר השירים and makes it into a kind of song, and one who reads a פסוק at a party at the wrong time, brings evil into the world. This is because the תורה puts on sackcloth, stands before הקדוש ברוך הוא, and says: Master of the world, Your children have made me like a harp that clowns play on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. Turning פסוקים into party songs or entertainment is condemned as bringing evil to the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases are listed: making שיר השירים into a secular song, and reciting any פסוק at a party just for fun. The reason is given as a picture: the תורה dresses in mourning clothes and complains that she has been turned into a jester's musical instrument.

keyTerms.meaning: A banquet hall, a place of feasting
Girds herself in sackcloth, a sign of mourning

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who reads a verse of Song of Songs
and makes it into a kind of song,
and one who reads a verse in a banquet house
not at its proper time –
brings evil to the world,
because the Torah girds herself in sackcloth
and stands before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
and says before Him:
Master of the Universe,
Your children have made me like a harp
that jesters play on.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הַקּוֹרֵא פָּסוּק שֶׁל שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, loosely connected through the theme of feasting (מִשְׁתֶּה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turning פסוקים into secular songs or party entertainment brings evil to the world.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a main source for the idea that פסוקים must not be used as mere entertainment.

steps.title: Then what should they do while eating?
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא asks the תורה what people should engage in while they are eating and drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: My daughter, when they eat and drink, what should they busy themselves with?
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא responds to the תורה's complaint with a question. This sets up the תורה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes people will want some Torah content at their meals. If not songs from פסוקים, what is the right way? The answer follows.

phrases.english: He said to her: My daughter,
at the time that they eat and drink,
with what should they occupy themselves?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ בִּתִּי בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאוֹכְלִין וְשׁוֹתִין בַּמֶּה יִתְעַסְּקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the תורה's complaint in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What proper Torah activity is fitting during a meal.

steps.title: Each person should learn on his own level
steps.stepSummary: The תורה answers: people who know תנ״ך should learn תנ״ך; people who know משנה should learn משנה, הלכות and הגדות; people who know תלמוד should learn the laws of each festival on that festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said before Him: Master of the world, if they are masters of Scripture, let them learn תורה, נביאים and כתובים. If they are masters of משנה, let them learn משנה, הלכות and הגדות. And if they are masters of תלמוד, let them learn the laws of פסח on פסח, the laws of עצרת on עצרת, and the laws of the חג on the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The תורה answers הקדוש ברוך הוא's question. Instead of singing פסוקים, people should really learn, each at his own level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is sorted by level of knowledge: Scripture, then משנה, then תלמוד. For the highest level, the learning should fit the time, like the laws of each festival on that festival. This connects to the phrase 'בלא זמנו', not at its proper time, in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Masters of Scripture (people who know Tanach)

phrases.english: She said before Him: Master of the Universe,
if they are masters of Scripture –
let them engage in the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings.
If they are masters of Mishna –
let them engage in Mishna, in halakhot, and in aggadot.
And if they are masters of Talmud –
let them engage in the laws of Passover on Passover,
in the laws of Atzeret on Atzeret,
in the laws of the Festival on the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לְפָנָיו רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם אִם בַּעֲלֵי מִקְרָא הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At meals, each person should truly learn at his own level, and advanced learners should study the laws that fit the season.

steps.title: A פסוק at its proper time brings good
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, quoting רבי שמעון בן חנניא, teaches the positive side: reading a פסוק at its proper time brings good to the world, based on 'ודבר בעתו מה טוב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר testified in the name of רבי שמעון בן חנניא: Anyone who reads a פסוק at its proper time brings good to the world, as it says: 'And a word in its time, how good it is.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the positive side of the ברייתא: a פסוק said at the right time brings good to the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors the ברייתא exactly: 'בלא זמנו' brings רעה, while 'בזמנו' brings טובה. The proof is a פסוק in משלי praising a word spoken at its proper time.

keyTerms.meaning: In its season, at the right moment

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar testified
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥananya:
Anyone who reads a verse at its proper time
brings good to the world,
as it is stated: "And a word in its time, how good it is."

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the positive mirror image of the ברייתא's warning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading a פסוק at its proper time brings good to the world.
steps.whatToRemember: Misusing a פסוק (as a song or party entertainment, 'not at its time') brings רעה. Using it at its proper time brings טובה.

steps.title: Whispering over a wound: only when he spits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of one who whispers over a wound. רבי יוחנן says this applies when he also spits, because ה׳'s name may not be mentioned over spit.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who whispers over a wound, etc.' רבי יוחנן said: And only when he spits on it, because one may not mention the name of Heaven over spit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה: someone who whispers פסוקים over a wound to heal it loses his share in עולם הבא. רבי יוחנן explains which case is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן narrows the case to someone who spits on the wound while whispering. Mentioning שם שמים together with spitting is disrespect to ה׳, and that is why the punishment is so severe.

keyTerms.meaning: One who whispers (a charm or פסוק) over a wound
Etc.: the rest of the quoted line
The name of Heaven, ה׳'s name

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying whispering for healing is always permitted. He is defining which case gets the משנה's harsh punishment of losing עולם הבא: whispering together with spitting.

phrases.english: And one who whispers over a wound, etc.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And (this is) when he spits on it,
because one does not mention the name of Heaven
over spitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַלּוֹחֵשׁ עַל הַמַּכָּה וְכוּ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the aggadic material to explaining the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's whisperer over a wound is one who also spits, since ה׳'s name may not be mentioned over spit.

steps.title: Even פסוקים without ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: It was stated: רב says even the פסוק 'נגע צרעת' is included, and רבי חנינא says even 'ויקרא אל משה' is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב said, even 'a mark of צרעת'. רבי חנינא said: even 'And He called to משה'.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain how far the משנה's prohibition reaches: even פסוקים that don't contain ה׳'s name are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says even a פסוק about the illness itself that has no name of ה׳, like 'נגע צרעת', is forbidden. רבי חנינא goes further: even a פסוק with nothing to do with the illness, like 'ויקרא אל משה', is forbidden. Each 'אפילו' widens the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces statements of אמוראים)
A mark of צרעת (a skin affliction)

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav said,
Even "a mark of tzara'at."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:9. This פסוק has no name of ה׳ in it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Even "And He called to Moses."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:1. This is a פסוק that has nothing to do with sickness at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר רַב אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ נֶגַע צָרַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the scope of the משנה's case explained in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: even a פסוק without ה׳'s name, like 'נגע צרעת', is included. רבי חנינא: even an unrelated פסוק, like 'ויקרא אל משה', is included.

steps.title: Soothing actions allowed on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא permits three soothing actions on שבת: smearing and rubbing the stomach, whispering charms for snake and scorpion bites, and passing a vessel over the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: On שבת you may smear oil on the stomach area and rub it. You may whisper the charm for snakes and scorpions. You may pass a vessel over a sore eye.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after discussing whispering over a wound, the גמרא brings a ברייתא listing things you may do on שבת to ease pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Healing on שבת is normally limited, but these actions are permitted. The list includes rubbing, whispering a charm, and passing a vessel over the eye. That last item gets a limit in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught: opens a ברייתא
A whispered charm for snake and scorpion bites

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may smear oil on and rub the intestinal area on Shabbat,
and one may whisper the charm for snakes and scorpions on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַעֲבִירִין כְּלִי עַל גַּב הָעַיִן בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: and one may pass a vessel over the eye on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: סָכִין וּמְמַשְׁמְשִׁין בִּבְנֵי מֵעַיִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whispering over a wound to a ברייתא about soothing actions and charms on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rubbing the stomach, whispering charms for bites, and passing a vessel over the eye are all allowed on שבת.

steps.title: Only a vessel that may be moved
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the vessel rule: only a vessel that may be moved on שבת may be passed over the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: When is this allowed? With a vessel you may move on שבת. With a vessel you may not move on שבת, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a limit to the last item in the ברייתא, the vessel over the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The soothing action itself is fine, but the vessel must be one that may be handled on שבת. A vessel that is מוקצה stays forbidden even for this.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case were these words said? Introduces a limit
A vessel that may be moved on שבת
A vessel that may not be moved on שבת (מוקצה)

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In what case are these words said?
With a vessel that may be moved,
but with a vessel that may not be moved, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the vessel case from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Passing a vessel over the eye on שבת is allowed only with a vessel that may be moved.

steps.title: Asking demons on Shabbat and on weekdays
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא forbids asking demons on שבת, and רבי יוסי says it is forbidden even on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not ask demons for information on שבת. רבי יוסי says: even on a weekday it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more rule, about asking demons, and רבי יוסי disagrees by making it stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion forbids asking demons only on שבת, which suggests it is allowed on a weekday. רבי יוסי forbids it every day. The reason for his strictness is explained in step 14.

phrases.english: And one may not consult demons on Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף בַּחוֹל אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: Even on a weekday it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין שׁוֹאֲלִין בִּדְבַר שֵׁדִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new rule and a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Asking demons is forbidden on שבת; רבי יוסי forbids it on weekdays too.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so asking demons is forbidden even on weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא decides the dispute from the ברייתא in favor of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the הלכה is like רבי יוסי, one should not ask demons even on a weekday. The next line explains why רבי יוסי says this.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The word אֵין in round brackets is left out of the corrected text. Read it as 'the הלכה IS like רבי יוסי', not 'is not'.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word אֵין ('not') in round brackets, but the corrected wording leaves it out, so the הלכה is like רבי יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Asking demons is forbidden even on weekdays, like רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's reason is danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי forbids asking demons on weekdays only because it is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even רבי יוסי only said it because of danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רבי יוסי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think רבי יוסי treats asking demons as forbidden witchcraft. The גמרא says no: the problem is danger, because the demons might harm the person. The next step gives a story to show this danger.

phrases.english: And even Rabbi Yosei did not say it
except because of danger,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֹא אֲמָרָהּ אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם סַכָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the opinion that was just ruled as הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי's ban on asking demons on weekdays is based on danger.

steps.title: The story of רב יצחק בר יוסף and the cedar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the danger: רב יצחק בר יוסף was swallowed into a cedar tree, and only a miracle split the tree open to free him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like what happened to רב יצחק בר יוסף: he was swallowed into a cedar tree. A miracle happened for him, the cedar split open and spit him out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real event to show how dangerous dealing with demons can be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story backs up the claim in step 14 that the problem is danger. Getting swallowed by a tree shows real physical harm, and he was saved only by a miracle.
steps.whatToRemember: Asking demons is forbidden even on weekdays, like רבי יוסי, and the reason is the real danger they bring.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Like that incident of Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef,
who was swallowed into a cedar tree,
and a miracle was done for him:
the cedar split open and spat him out.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case to support the danger reason.
steps.raayaObject: That dealing with demons is physically dangerous.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of רב יצחק בר יוסף swallowed by a cedar.

steps.title: Rubbing the stomach, but not in the weekday way
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows smearing and rubbing the stomach on שבת, but only if it is not done the normal weekday way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: You may smear oil on the stomach and rub it on שבת, as long as you do not do it the way you do on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that repeats the rubbing rule but adds a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said rubbing the stomach is allowed. This ברייתא adds that it must look different from a weekday. The condition is not explained yet, so the next step asks how to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: As long as, on condition that

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may smear oil on and rub the intestinal area on Shabbat,
provided that he does not do it
the way he does it on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶׂה כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה בַּחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the rubbing rule from step 10 and adds a condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rubbing the stomach on שבת is allowed only in a way different from weekdays.

steps.title: How should it be done?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how exactly to rub the stomach on שבת so that it is different from a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: what is the 'different way'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a condition without saying how to keep it. This question asks for the practical method.

phrases.english: How does he do it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical meaning of the condition in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What way of rubbing counts as different from a weekday.

steps.title: Two ways to change from the weekday way
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says first smear and then rub; רבי יוחנן says smear and rub at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: He smears first, and afterwards rubs. רבי יוחנן said: He smears and rubs at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question, each giving a different way to change from the weekday method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each answer says the שבת way is the opposite of the usual weekday way. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא wants smearing first and rubbing after. רבי יוחנן wants both done together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
He smears oil and afterwards rubs.
Rabbi Yochanan said:
He smears oil and rubs at the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: סָךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְמַשְׁמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either smear first and then rub (רבי חמא ברבי חנינא), or smear and rub together (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: Demons of oil and eggs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one may consult demons of oil and demons of eggs, but they lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Demons of oil and demons of eggs, you are allowed to consult them, but they lie.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about certain kinds of demons that people would consult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the danger of demons in step 14, these are permitted to consult. The catch is practical: they do not tell the truth, so asking them is pointless.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Demons of oil and demons of eggs,
it is permitted to consult them,
but because they lie, it is useless.
phrases.notes: The words 'it is useless' are not written; the ברייתא just means: allowed, but they lie.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׂרֵי שֶׁמֶן וְשָׂרֵי בֵיצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of consulting demons with a new ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consulting demons of oil and eggs is allowed, but they are not reliable.

steps.title: Whispering over oil in a vessel versus in the hand
steps.stepSummary: One may whisper over oil in a vessel but not over oil in the hand; therefore, one may smear from oil in a hand but not from oil in a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may whisper over oil in a vessel, but you may not whisper over oil in a hand. So you may smear yourself with oil from a hand, but you may not smear with oil from a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a rule about whispering over oil and a practical result about which oil to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whispering is done over oil in a vessel, not oil in a hand. So oil brought in a vessel might have had a whisper said over it and could cause harm, while oil in a hand has no such worry. That is why the safe choice is oil from a hand.
steps.confusionAlert: The order flips: you WHISPER over oil in a vessel, so you SMEAR from oil in a hand. Don't mix up the two halves.
steps.whatToRemember: Oil in a vessel may have a whisper on it, so one smears only from oil in a hand.

phrases.english: One may whisper over oil that is in a vessel,
and one may not whisper over oil that is in the hand.
Therefore, one may smear with oil that is in a hand,
and one may not smear with oil that is in a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹחֲשִׁין עַל שֶׁמֶן שֶׁבִּכְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא about oil and charms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whispering works on oil in a vessel, not in a hand; so one smears only from oil in a hand.

steps.title: רב יצחק's boils from oil in a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא smeared oil from a vessel, got boils, and was healed by a woman's whispered remedy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא came to an inn. They gave him oil in a vessel. He smeared it, and boils broke out on his face. In the market, a woman said she saw the spirit of חמת on him. She did something for him, and he was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows why smearing oil from a vessel is dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said oil in a vessel can be whispered over, so you should not smear from it. Here someone smeared oil from a vessel and was harmed, which shows the danger is real. The woman's remedy shows that this kind of harm can also be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: An inn, a place to stay

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta
happened to come to a certain inn.
They brought him oil in a vessel.
He smeared it, and boils broke out on his face.
He went out to the market.
A certain woman saw him and said:
I see the spirit of חמת here.
phrases.notes: חמת is the name of a harmful spirit.

phrases.english: She did something for him, and he was healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא אִיקְּלַע לְהָהוּא אוּשְׁפִּיזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the danger of oil in a vessel taught in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one should not smear from oil in a vessel
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא getting boils

steps.title: If ה׳ places no disease, why does He need to heal?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא points out that the פסוק says ה׳ will not place disease on us, yet calls Him our Healer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to רבה בר מרי: The פסוק says, "All the disease I placed in Egypt I will not place on you, for I am ה׳ your Healer." If He does not place disease on us, why do we need healing?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא raises a problem inside one פסוק: the two halves seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half promises no disease at all. The second half calls ה׳ our Healer, which only makes sense if there is disease. So the פסוק seems to contradict itself.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Rabba bar Mari:
It is written: "All the disease that I placed in Egypt

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָשִׂים עָלֶיךָ כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ רֹפְאֶךָ״,
phrases.english: I will not place upon you, for I am ה׳ your Healer."
But since He does not place it,
why is healing needed?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁלֹּא שָׂם, רְפוּאָה לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of healing remedies to a פסוק about ה׳ as Healer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A promise of no disease makes the description of ה׳ as Healer seem unnecessary.

steps.title: The verse explains itself: disease only if we don't listen
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the promise depends on listening to ה׳; if we don't listen, disease comes, but ה׳ still heals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר מרי answered in the name of רבי יוחנן: This פסוק explains itself. It starts, "If you will surely listen to the voice of ה׳ your God." If you listen, I will not place disease. If you don't listen, I will. Even so, "I am ה׳ your Healer."
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered by reading the beginning of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise of no disease is conditional: it only applies if we listen to ה׳. If we don't listen, disease can come, and that is where ה׳ as Healer comes in. So the two halves fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains itself, can be understood from its own words

steps.whatToRemember: Even when ה׳ sends sickness because we did not listen, He is still our Healer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
This verse explains itself,
as it says: "And He said: If you will surely listen
to the voice of ה׳ your God" —
phrases.notes: These words are the start of the very same פסוק.

phrases.english: If you listen, I will not place it,
and if you do not listen, I will place it.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן, ״כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ רֹפְאֶךָ״.
phrases.english: Even so, "for I am ה׳ your Healer."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְרָא זֶה מֵעַצְמוֹ נִדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the verse in context: the promise is conditional
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק promises no disease at all, making healing pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: No disease only if we listen; if not, disease comes, and ה׳ still heals.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר is sick: the students cry and רבי עקיבא laughs
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אליעזר was ill, his students cried, but רבי עקיבא laughed, and they asked him why.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: When רבי אליעזר got sick, his students came to visit. He told them, "There is fierce anger in the world." They began crying, but רבי עקיבא laughed. They asked why he laughed. He asked why they were crying. They said, "Can a ספר תורה be in pain and we not cry?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about רבי אליעזר's illness. It sets up the question of why רבי עקיבא laughed, which he answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students see their rebbi's suffering as a tragedy, like a ספר תורה being hurt. רבי עקיבא's laughter seems shocking, so the story builds tension for his explanation.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said:
When Rabbi Eliezer fell ill,
his students came in to visit him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: חֵמָה עַזָּה יֵשׁ בָּעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: He said to them: There is fierce anger in the world.
phrases.notes: He means Heavenly anger is what is causing his suffering.

phrases.english: They began to cry,
and Rabbi Akiva was laughing.
They said to him: Why are you laughing?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתֶּם בּוֹכִים?
phrases.english: He said to them: And why are you crying?
They said to him: Is it possible that a Torah scroll
is in pain and we will not cry?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: כְּשֶׁחָלָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of sickness with a new story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The story sets up why רבי עקיבא laughed at his rebbi's suffering.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא explains: suffering means reward is saved for later
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says he worried that רבי אליעזר's constant success meant he was getting all his reward in this world; now that he suffers, he is happy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: That is exactly why I laugh. As long as I saw that my rebbi's wine never soured, his flax never got ruined, his oil never spoiled, and his honey never went bad, I thought maybe, God forbid, he was getting all his reward in this world. Now that I see him suffering, I am happy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers the students' question and explains his laughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Perfect success in this world could mean a person is being paid his full reward now, with less left for עולם הבא. Suffering shows that he is being cleaned of small sins here, so his reward in עולם הבא stays complete. So what looks sad is actually good news.

keyTerms.meaning: Received his world, got his reward already

phrases.english: He said to them: That is why I am laughing.
As long as I saw my teacher

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין יֵינוֹ מַחְמִיץ וְאֵין פִּשְׁתָּנוֹ לוֹקֶה
phrases.english: that his wine did not sour and his flax was not ruined,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין שַׁמְנוֹ מַבְאִישׁ וְאֵין דּוּבְשָׁנוֹ מַדְבִּישׁ,
phrases.english: and his oil did not go bad and his honey did not spoil,
I said: perhaps, God forbid,
my teacher has received his world.
phrases.notes: He means he was getting all his reward here, leaving less for עולם הבא.

phrases.english: But now that I see my teacher in pain,
I am happy.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכָךְ אֲנִי מְשַׂחֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question from step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי עקיבא laughed at his rebbi's suffering
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suffering in this world shows that his reward in עולם הבא is saved in full.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר asks: did I miss anything in the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר challenges רבי עקיבא: what sin could he need to pay for, if he kept the whole Torah?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: עקיבא, did I leave out anything from the whole תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר pushes back on רבי עקיבא's idea that he is being punished for sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's answer assumes his rebbi has some sins to pay for. רבי אליעזר challenges that: he kept all of the Torah, so why should he suffer?

keyTerms.meaning: Anything at all (here, used as a question: did I...?)

phrases.english: He said to him: Akiva,
did I leave out anything from the entire Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲקִיבָא, כְּלוּם חִיסַּרְתִּי מִן הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in רבי עקיבא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's assumption that רבי אליעזר has sins to pay for
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he kept the entire Torah, there is nothing to atone for through suffering.

steps.title: No righteous person never sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers with a פסוק his rebbi taught: there is no righteous person who never sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: You taught us, our rebbi: "For there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers his rebbi's challenge using a פסוק from קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the greatest צדיק has some small sins, because no person is perfect. So suffering can still clean those away. רבי עקיבא cleverly uses a teaching he learned from רבי אליעזר himself.
steps.whatToRemember: No person is completely free of sin, so even a צדיק's suffering can be a kindness that saves his reward for עולם הבא.

phrases.english: He said to him: You taught us, our teacher:
"For there is no righteous man on earth
who does good and does not sin."

steps.triggerLanguage: לִימַּדְתָּנוּ רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a פסוק that no person is free of sin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Someone who kept the whole Torah has no sins to atone for.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every person sins sometimes, so even a great צדיק can benefit from suffering.

steps.title: Four elders come to visit the sick רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that when רבי אליעזר was sick, four sages came to visit him: רבי טרפון, רבי יהושע, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When רבי אליעזר became sick, four elders came in to visit him: רבי טרפון, רבי יהושע, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets the scene for a new story. It names who came to visit, which prepares us for what each one will say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a separate account of a visit to the sick רבי אליעזר, this time from a ברייתא and with four named elders instead of his students. The list matters because each visitor will speak in turn, and רבי עקיבא is named last.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (this opens a ברייתא)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
When Rabbi Eliezer became sick,
four elders went in to visit him:
Rabbi Tarfon, and Rabbi Yehoshua,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, and Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֶׁחָלָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה בר בר חנה's account, the גמרא brings a separate ברייתא about a visit to the sick רבי אליעזר, which also ends with רבי עקיבא's view on suffering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four sages came to visit רבי אליעזר when he was sick.

steps.title: רבי טרפון says he is better than rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון tells רבי אליעזר that he is better for the Jewish people than a drop of rain. Rain helps only in this world, but he helps in this world and the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון spoke up and said: You are better for the Jewish people than a drop of rain. A drop of rain helps in this world, but my teacher helps in this world and in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The first visitor, רבי טרפון, praises the sick רבי אליעזר by comparing him to rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain is about the most valuable thing for life in this world. רבי טרפון says רבי אליעזר is worth even more, because his Torah helps people in this world and also in עולם הבא. This sets the pattern the next two visitors will follow.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon spoke up and said:
You are better for the Jewish people
than a drop of rain,
because a drop of rain helps in this world,
but my teacher helps in this world and in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first of the four visitors named in step 28 speaks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר is better than rain, because he helps in both worlds.

steps.title: רבי יהושע says he is better than the sun
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע uses the same pattern. רבי אליעזר is better for the Jewish people than the sun, which helps only in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע spoke up and said: You are better for the Jewish people than the sun. The sun helps in this world, but my teacher helps in this world and in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The second visitor, רבי יהושע, gives his own praise, this time comparing רבי אליעזר to the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure is exactly like רבי טרפון's. Only the comparison changes, from rain to the sun. Each visitor picks something even more basic to life, and still says רבי אליעזר is worth more because his help reaches עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The sphere of the sun, meaning the sun itself

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua spoke up and said:
You are good for the Jewish people
more than the sphere of the sun,
because the sun helps in this world,
but my teacher helps in this world and in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second visitor follows the same pattern as רבי טרפון, with a new comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר is better than the sun, because he helps in both worlds.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says he is better than a father and mother
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses the same pattern. רבי אליעזר is better for the Jewish people than a father and mother, who help only in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה spoke up and said: You are better for the Jewish people than a father and mother. A father and mother help in this world, but my teacher helps in this world and in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The third visitor, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, gives the last of the three similar praises, comparing רבי אליעזר to parents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Parents give a child life and raise him, but only for this world. A rebbi who teaches Torah brings a person to עולם הבא too, so רבי אליעזר is called greater than parents. With this, three of the four visitors have spoken, and all of them tried to comfort him with praise.

keyTerms.meaning: And my teacher (said respectfully about רבי אליעזר)
You are better (literally: you are good)

steps.whatToRemember: Three visitors, one pattern: rain, then the sun, then parents. Each helps only in this world, while רבי אליעזר helps in this world and in עולם הבא. רבי עקיבא, the fourth visitor, has not spoken yet.

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya spoke up and said:
You are good for the Jewish people
more than a father and mother,
because a father and mother help in this world,
but my teacher helps in this world and in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third visitor completes the series of matching praises.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר is better than a father and mother, because he helps in both worlds.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא says suffering is precious
steps.stepSummary: Unlike the other three visitors, רבי עקיבא does not praise רבי אליעזר. He says that יסורין are precious.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא responded and said: Suffering is precious.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא is the fourth visitor to speak. Instead of praising רבי אליעזר, he says that suffering is something precious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three sages all used the same pattern: 'you are better than rain, the sun, or parents.' רבי עקיבא breaks the pattern. Rather than comforting רבי אליעזר by praising him, he gives his pain a positive meaning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva responded and said:
Suffering is precious.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth visitor speaks. He breaks the praise pattern of steps 29 to 31 with a new idea.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר asks to be propped up to hear רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks the people around him to support him so he can hear what his student רבי עקיבא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Support me, and I will hear the words of עקיבא my student, who said, 'Suffering is precious.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר reacts to רבי עקיבא's words. He asks to be helped up so he can listen closely. This sets up his question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The praise from the other sages did not move him. רבי עקיבא's idea makes the sick man want to sit up. This shows that the idea of suffering being precious really spoke to him.

phrases.english: He said to them: Support me,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר talking. He is sick in bed and wants to be helped up to sit.

phrases.english: and I will hear the words of Akiva my student,
who said: Suffering is precious.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: סַמְּכוּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אליעזר reacts to רבי עקיבא's statement from step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר wants to hear רבי עקיבא's idea more closely.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks רבי עקיבא where he learned that suffering is precious.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: עקיבא, from where do you know this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר asks his student for a source. Where in the תורה do we see that suffering is precious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real request for a source, not an attack. Even on his sickbed, the rebbi wants a proof from a פסוק and not just a nice saying.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do you know this? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: He said to him: Akiva,
this, from where do you have it?

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ מִנַּיִן לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listening, רבי אליעזר asks for the source of רבי עקיבא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows suffering is precious.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא begins his proof from King מנשה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא starts to answer with the פסוק saying that מנשה became king at twelve, ruled fifty-five years, and did evil. He then begins to quote a second פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I am explaining a פסוק: 'מנשה was twelve years old when he became king, and he ruled fifty-five years in Jerusalem... and he did what was evil in the eyes of ה׳.' And it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא begins his answer by quoting a פסוק about the wicked King מנשה. Then he starts a second פסוק. The proof is not finished here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק sets the scene: מנשה was a long-ruling king who did evil. The words 'and it is written' tell us a second פסוק is coming. רבי עקיבא's point will come from putting the two פסוקים together.

keyTerms.meaning: I am explaining (learning from) a פסוק
מנשה, the wicked king of יהודה, son of חזקיהו
and it is written (a second פסוק is coming)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the proof to be complete yet. The amud ends on 'and it is written', so the key second פסוק comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: He said: I am explaining a verse:
"Menashe was twelve years old when he began to reign,
and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem
[etc.] and he did what was evil in the eyes of ה׳,"
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. It means 'and so on', skipping the rest of the פסוק and jumping ahead.

phrases.english: and it is written:

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְרָא אֲנִי דּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא begins answering the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source comes from the פסוקים about King מנשה. The answer is only started here and continues on the next amud.
